The '''Old Franklin County Jail''' is a historic [[jail]] located at [[Chambersburg, Pennsylvania|Chambersburg]] in [[Franklin County, Pennsylvania]]. It was built in 1818, and is a two-story, brick building with a [[slate]] covered hipped roof topped by a [[cupola]].  The original building measures 84 feet wide by 48 feet deep.  In 1880, a cell block was added.  The jail yard is divided into two sections and surrounded by a 20-foot-high wall.<ref name=nrhpdoc>{{cite report|type=none|url=https://catalog.archives.gov/id/71994969 |title=National Register of Historic Places Registration: Pennsylvania SP Franklin County Jail|publisher=National Archives and Records Administration |author= Murray E. Kauffman| date = September 1969 | access-date=December 20, 2025 }} ({{NationalArchivesNote}})</ref> At least five prisoners were hanged on the premises.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://articles.herald-mail.com/2000-08-06/news/25143410_1_gallows-humor-trap-door-executions | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304111956/http://articles.herald-mail.com/2000-08-06/news/25143410_1_gallows-humor-trap-door-executions | url-status=dead | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | title=Gallows refurbished in Pa. | work=The Herald-Mail | date=August 6, 2000 | accessdate=2 December 2015 | author=Aines, Don}}</ref>

Now known as the '''Old Jail''', the building houses a museum and genealogical library operated by the Franklin County Historical Society - Kittochtinny.

It was listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1970. It is included in the [[Chambersburg Historic District]].<ref name="nris"/>
